claim_verdicts.evidence: l.53: a call "that isn't immediately awaited returns a Task<int>"; l.66: "the exception is stored in the returned task. The exception is rethrown when the task is awaited." Together: the task stands for work under way and ends holding the result or the failure; Task<TResult> carries a TResult.

common-async-bugs l.23: "Adding the `async` keyword to a method doesn't make the method run on a background thread. It tells the compiler to allow `await` inside the method body and to wrap the return value in a Task." top-level-statements l.37-38: `await` and `return` -> "static async Task<int> Main"; `await` -> "static async Task Main". Lesson says only "an async entry point".

"When you invoke an async method, it runs synchronously until it reaches the first `await` on an incomplete awaitable. If the method contains no `await` expressions, or if every awaitable it awaits is already complete, the method completes entirely on the calling thread"

"An `await` expression in an async method doesn't block the current thread while the awaited task is running. Instead, the expression signs up the rest of the method as a continuation and returns control to the caller of the async method." RunAsync itself awaits, so the same holds one level up; lesson §4 now names the second thread as the caller's.

"In a console app, SynchronizationContext.Current returns `null`. When a method yields at an `await`, the continuation runs on whatever thread pool thread is available"; l.37: "Thread 1 (the main thread) appears only once ... All subsequent iterations run on thread pool threads."
"The type of expression `await t` is `TResult` if the type of expression `t` is Task<TResult> or ValueTask<TResult>. ... In both cases, if `t` throws an exception, `await t` rethrows the exception."

l.109: "If you call a task-returning method in an `async` method without awaiting it, the method starts the asynchronous operation but doesn't wait for it to complete. The compiler warns you about this case with `CS4014`". Awaiting later is valid: TAP model starts getStringTask and awaits it after independent work.

Rerun this round was denied by the sandbox.
"If a method that returns a Task or Task<TResult> throws an exception, the exception is stored in the returned task. The exception is rethrown when the task is awaited."

"It happens when you synchronously block (call Wait, Task<TResult>.Result, or GetAwaiter().GetResult()) on a thread that has a single-threaded SynchronizationContext." Wait and Result are named as synchronous blocking.

l.56: "Code on the UI thread ... calls an async method and blocks on the returned task." l.57: awaits "without using `ConfigureAwait(false)`" (the default). l.58-59: "the continuation tries to post back to the original SynchronizationContext. That context's thread is blocked waiting for the task to complete—deadlock." Console: "SynchronizationContext.Current returns `null`".

TPL exceptions l.16: "the Task infrastructure wraps them in an AggregateException instance"; l.18: "Even if only one exception is thrown, it is still wrapped in an AggregateException exception". Parallel-loop doc l.25: "an AggregateException with an OperationCanceledException as an `InnerException`". async-scenarios l.250: Result/Wait "wraps exceptions in AggregateException".

await.md l.28: "You can use the `await` operator only in a method, lambda expression, or anonymous method that is modified by the async keyword." "The Task<TResult> return type is used for an async method that contains a return statement in which the operand is `TResult`." LoadPaidOrdersAsync l.27 `return orders;` with orders : List<string>.

issues.quote: sends the `SELECT` and waits once more; when the rows arrive it fills the list and marks the task finished
issues.text: Section 4 and the diagram (one "rows" arrow) make it sound like all rows come back in one wait, then the list is filled. Section 5 then says "the method may stop and resume once per row". I could reconcile it, but I stopped to check whether I had misread section 4.
issues.fix: In section 4, change to "…and waits once more; as the rows arrive, one at a time, it fills the list, and after the last one it marks the task finished."

issues.quote: if that is the thread you are holding, the rest never runs and the program stops for good.
issues.text: "Stops for good" read to me first as "crashes and exits". Only in section 6 ("window freezes with no error at all") did I learn it means it hangs. The chain ".Result waits for the rest; the rest waits for the thread .Result holds" is also left for me to assemble.
issues.fix: Replace "the program stops for good" with "the program hangs: each side waits for the other, and nothing reports an error".

issues.quote: so the two halves of your code now run in an order nobody chose
issues.text: "The two halves" is not named anywhere before; I guessed it means the code after my call and the rest of the method I forgot to await, but I had to re-read the bullet.
issues.fix: Name them: "so the lines after your call and the rest of the method you called now run in an order nobody chose".
